name: acta-fit
description: Acta Fit is a strength-training log for iPhone and Apple Watch. This plugin reads the signed-in user's own workouts, records, training stats, heart rate and power, and files training-plan and workout proposals that the user reviews and accepts inside the app.

positive.prompt: What did I do in my last three workouts?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the three most recent sessions with date, title, completed sets and volume in the user's unit, then details the exercises and sets of each from get_workout.

positive.prompt: How has my squat progressed over the last two months?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the squat sets over the period and describes the top-set and estimated one-rep-max trend. Warm-up sets are flagged and left out of the trend.

positive.description: Per-set heart rate for the latest session
positive.prompt: What was my average heart rate during each set of my most recent workout?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the latest session, calls get_workout_metrics with its session_key and reports heart rate per set. If power is absent it is explained from the tool's notes, never reported as zero watts.

positive.description: Monthly volume against the user's typical month
positive.prompt: How much total volume did I lift this month compared with my typical month?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_training_stats for the month and 3months periods and compares workout count, sets and total volume in the user's unit.

positive.description: Training-plan proposal built from the user's own lifts
positive.prompt: Build me a 3-day upper/lower plan using my current lifts and training maxes.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the user's templates and training maxes first, files exactly one proposal with create_training_plan, tells the user to review it in the Acta Fit app, and get_plan_inbox shows the proposal as pending. No workout data changes.

negative.description: General nutrition advice. The plugin holds no nutrition data, so it should not be called; the assistant answers from general knowledge.
negative.prompt: What's a good macro split for cutting?

negative.description: Exercise-science explanation. Nothing in the user's log is needed, so no tool is called and the assistant answers directly.
Out-of-scope action. The plugin has no booking, scheduling or third-party integrations, so the assistant says it cannot book sessions and calls no tool.
negative.prompt: Book me a personal trainer session at my gym tomorrow.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing. Acta Fit memberships are bought inside the iOS app through Apple's in-app purchase.

publication.release_notes: First release of the Acta Fit plugin: read workouts, exercise history, training stats, plans, templates, training maxes, and heart-rate and power analysis; propose training plans, single workouts and new exercises for approval in the app.

interface.longDescription:
Acta Fit is a strength and conditioning log for iPhone and Apple Watch. Connect it to ask about your own training data in plain language.

What you can ask:
- Your recent workouts: dates, exercises, sets, reps, loads and volume.
- Progress on any lift: top sets and estimated one-rep-max trends over time.
- Training stats for the week, month or year: workout count, sets, volume and weeks active.
- Heart rate and power for any session, including per-set and per-interval breakdowns, time in zone and normalized power, whenever your Apple Watch or another Apple Health source recorded them.
- Your plans, saved workout templates and training maxes.

What it can propose:
- A training plan, a single workout, or a new exercise. Proposals land in the Acta Fit app, where you review and accept or dismiss them. Nothing in your log changes until you accept.

Requirements: the Acta Fit iPhone app with an account and AI sync turned on. Weights are shown in your own unit.
capabilities: Read workout history, personal records, volume and training stats
Heart-rate and power analysis per session, set or interval
Propose training plans and single workouts for approval in the app
Register new exercise names for future proposals
